recipes.title: Fried Green Plantains with Nectarine Salsa

ingredients: 1/4 cup ghee, lard, or olive oil
steps: In a large bowl, combine the cassava flour, arrowroot and salt. Work in the fat with your fingers until fully incorporated, then add the water and knead until a ball of dough forms.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a ball, and keep the bowl covered so they don't dry out.
Flatten each ball between parchment or plastic wrap with a rolling pin, tortilla press, or heavy books.
Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium-high.
Cook each tortilla about 1 minute until bubbles form, flip, and cook 1 minute more until lightly browned on both sides.
Stack on a plate under a clean towel until ready to eat.
tips: Don't confuse cassava flour with tapioca flour: tapioca makes these super-gummy. Both come from cassava root, but cassava flour is the whole dried root.
Keep the dough balls covered so they stay moist.
Freeze cooked tortillas between parchment sheets for up to 6 months.

ai.cliffNotes: Cassava-and-arrowroot dough pressed thin and griddled a minute per side: real paleo taco tortillas.
keyTips: Buy cassava flour (Otto's is the common brand), NOT tapioca starch.
Use olive oil as the fat for the heart-healthy version.
Dry, hot pan, no oil: wait for bubbles before flipping.

Pressure Cooker / Slow Cooker Kalua Pig

ingredients: 1 (3 1/2-pound) boneless pork shoulder roast, tied with butcher's twine
3 scallions, trimmed and cut into 3-inch segments
1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch coins
2 heads butter, green leaf, or romaine lettuce, washed, spun dry and separated into leaves
steps: Pat the pork dry. Mix the salt and coconut sugar and rub it all over the roast, into every nook.
Refrigerate the roast uncovered in a large bowl for at least 8 hours or up to 3 days.
When ready to cook, pat the pork dry. Heat 1 tablespoon ghee on the pressure cooker's Sauté setting (medium-high for stovetop).
Sear the roast on 3 sides, about 2 minutes undisturbed per side, leaving the top (skin/fat side) unbrowned.
Add the scallions, garlic, ginger and 1/2 cup water (1 cup for stovetop); pressure-cook on high 2 hours (stovetop: 1 1/2 hours).
Turn off the cooker and let the pressure release naturally; if it hasn't come down after 15 minutes, release it manually. Check the roast is fork-tender (if not, 30 more minutes at high pressure).
Turn on the broiler to high with the rack in the lower-middle; set a wire rack on a foil-lined rimmed baking sheet.
Remove the twine and set the pork fat-side up on the rack. Pour the cooking liquid into a large cup and skim off the fat; you should have about 2 cups of pork jus.
Broil the roast 5 to 10 minutes, basting with the jus, until nicely browned. Transfer to a platter.
Shred the pork and pour more jus over it. Serve with lettuce, Cauli Rice, kimchi, pickles and Fauxchujang: pile it on a lettuce leaf, spoon on Fauxchujang, wrap and eat.
tips: Bo ssäm means 'wrapped' or 'packaged': slow-cooked pork with a crunchy exterior, spicy sauce, kimchi, pickles and rice, all in lettuce. A paleo shortcut of David Chang's Momofuku Ssäm Bar classic.
Dry-brine the salt-and-sugar rub at least 8 hours, up to 3 days, uncovered.

SWITCH IT UP, Slow Cooker Bo Ssäm (p.134): sear in a cast-iron skillet, then slow-cook on LOW with the scallions, ginger and garlic (no liquid needed) 9 to 12 hours until fork-tender; continue at the broiling step.
Extras keep 4 days refrigerated or 6 months frozen.

ai.cliffNotes: Salt-and-sugar-cured pork shoulder pressure-cooked 2 hours with aromatics, broiled crusty while basting with its own jus, then shredded into lettuce wraps with kimchi, pickles and Fauxchujang.
keyTips: Start the dry brine Thursday or Friday night: 8 hours minimum, and longer is better.
Leave the fat side unseared so it can blister under the broiler.
Skim the jus before basting; it's the seasoning for the shredded meat.
Kimchi and Fauxchujang bring the heat. Keep them on the side for the low-heat eater.

recipes.title: Pressure Cooker / Slow Cooker Carne Mechada

ingredients: 3 pounds flank steak, cut against the grain into 2-inch strips
1/2 cup Bone Broth (page 76) or chicken stock
steps: In a large bowl, toss the beef with the chili powder and 2 teaspoons salt; mix with your hands and set aside.
Heat the ghee in the pressure cooker (medium-high if stovetop). Add the onion, carrots, bell pepper and a sprinkle of salt; sauté 3 to 5 minutes until softened.
Add the tomato paste and garlic; stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the canned tomatoes, stock and fish sauce. Stir in the oregano and bay leaves.
Add the beef and stir to mix well.
Cover and cook under high pressure for 20 minutes (stovetop cooker: high heat to pressure, then low to maintain about 18 minutes).
Let the pressure release naturally (about 15 minutes). Transfer the beef to a serving bowl and shred with two forks.
Bring the sauce to a boil in the pot, skim off excess oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Discard the bay leaves, ladle the sauce over the meat, garnish with cilantro and serve.
tips: Like ropa vieja ('old clothes'), named for its resemblance to colorful rags: a Latin American stew of boiled, shredded flank steak. The pressure cooker cuts the usual hours in half.
SWITCH IT UP, Slow Cooker Carne Mechada: do steps 2 through 4 in a skillet, then cook everything in a slow cooker on LOW for 8 hours.
Let the pressure release naturally (~15 min); don't quick-release.
Skim the excess oil off the sauce before seasoning.
Keeps 4 days refrigerated or 4 months frozen.

ai.cliffNotes: Chili-rubbed flank strips pressure-cooked 20 minutes in a tomato, pepper and carrot sauce, then shredded and sauced: Latin shredded beef, no searing needed.
keyTips: Cut the flank against the grain into 2-inch strips before seasoning so it shreds into tender ribbons.
Natural release keeps the beef moist; a quick release squeezes it dry.
Skim the fat from the sauce, then taste: salt is easy to overdo with fish sauce in the pot.
Make-ahead friendly: it reheats well, which is why it sits in the Make-Ahead section.

Roast 30 minutes or until tender.
Spoon on Ginger Sesame Sauce and top with chives and sesame seeds.

Tastes great at room temperature and straight from the fridge, too.

ai.cliffNotes: Whole young carrots roasted until sweet, finished with a creamy ginger-sesame sauce, chives and sesame seeds.
keyTips: Pat the carrots dry so they roast instead of steam.

Grilled Balsamic Bok Choy with Golden Raisins

ingredients: 1/4 cup avocado oil or olive oil, plus extra for the grill
1/4 cup golden raisins, soaked in hot water 5 minutes until plump
steps: Heat a grill or grill pan to medium. Trim the woody ends of the bok choy, keeping the bunches intact, and halve them lengthwise.
Wash out any grit at the base, shake off the water, and lay them on a platter.
Drizzle with 1/4 cup oil and the salt; toss with your hands to coat.
Grease the hot grates with an oiled paper towel.
Grill cut-side down about 3 minutes until charred; flip and cook 3 minutes more until tender-crisp.
Season with pepper, drizzle with balsamic, and garnish with the raisins, almonds and mint.
tips: No grill or grill pan? Roast cut-side up on a lined baking sheet at 400°F for 20 minutes, then finish as in the last step.
Wash at the base, where dirt hides.

ai.cliffNotes: Halved baby bok choy charred on the grill, finished with balsamic, plump golden raisins, almonds and mint.
keyTips: Keep the bunches intact when trimming so the halves hold together on the grates.
The oven route (400°F, 20 min) works fine on a cold night.

ingredients: Grilled Balsamic Bok Choy (p.260) ingredients, minus the vinegar, raisins and almonds, plus:
steps: Follow Grilled Balsamic Bok Choy (p.260) through the grilling (or 400°F oven roast).
In the final step, skip the vinegar, raisins and almonds; drizzle with 1 teaspoon fish sauce and the juice of 1 lime.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and serve.
tips: SWITCH IT UP from the balsamic version for Asian flavors.
Same no-grill option: 400°F oven, 20 minutes, cut-side up.

ai.cliffNotes: Charred baby bok choy dressed with fish sauce and lime, finished with sesame seeds.
keyTips: Just 1 tsp fish sauce across 6 bunches keeps the sodium modest.
Dress it right before serving so the bok choy stays crisp.

ingredients: 1 tablespoon finely grated lemon zest (from 1 lemon)
2 medium carrots, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks
2 medium zucchini, cut into thin matchsticks
1/4 cup pitted green olives, roughly chopped
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F with the rack in the middle.
Whisk the harissa, honey and lemon zest; set aside half to brush on the cooked fish.
In a large bowl, combine the carrots, zucchini, olives, garlic, olive oil and lemon juice; season with salt and pepper.
Season the fish with salt and pepper, then brush 1/2 tablespoon of the harissa-honey on the top and sides of each fillet.
Fold 4 large squares of parchment in half and cut out hearts; open them flat and spread a quarter of the vegetables on one side of each crease.
Add a tablespoon of the pooled vegetable liquid, set a fillet on top harissa-side up, fold the parchment over, and crimp the edges tightly from the top center, twisting the point to seal.
Bake the packets on a rimmed sheet 10 to 15 minutes, to desired doneness.
Cut the packets open with shears straight out of the oven, brush on the remaining harissa-honey, garnish with sesame seeds and serve.
tips: Cooking in parchment gives delicate fish and tender vegetables in one packet: sweet, savory, spicy and tart.
Harissa is a Tunisian hot chile paste; sriracha subs if you can't find it.
Pro tip: don't let the fish's internal temperature rise above 145°F.

ai.cliffNotes: Salmon brushed with honey-harissa and steamed in parchment over lemony carrot, zucchini and green olive matchsticks, then glazed again at the table.
keyTips: Low-heat house: keep your wife's packet harissa-free (honey + lemon zest only) and pass the harissa glaze at the table.
Crimp the parchment tightly; the trapped steam is what cooks the vegetables.
Pull at 10 minutes for 1 1/2-inch fillets and check; 145°F max.

ingredients: 6 dried shiitake mushrooms, reconstituted in a bowl of water for at least 1 hour
1 tablespoon ghee, avocado oil, or olive oil
1 (2-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch coins
1 cup Bone Broth (page 76) or chicken stock
steps: Rinse the dried mushrooms and soak them in water at least 1 hour ahead (or use fresh mushrooms if pressed for time).
Heat the oven to 450°F with the rack in the middle; heat a 12-inch oven-safe skillet over medium.
Heat the fat, add the shallots and a sprinkle of salt, and cook 5 to 10 minutes until softened. Meanwhile, salt the thighs liberally on both sides (about 2 teaspoons total).
Squeeze the mushrooms dry, trim the woody stems, and thinly slice the caps.
Add the mushrooms, ginger and garlic to the shallots; stir 1 minute until aromatic, then move the vegetables to a plate and wipe out the pan.
Over medium-high, sear the chicken skin-side down 4 to 5 minutes until browned and crispy, peppering the meaty side; flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Stir the fish sauce into the broth and pour it into the pan without wetting the crispy skin; tuck the shallots, mushrooms and garlic between the pieces.
Roast 15 to 20 minutes until the thighs reach 165°F.
Taste the sauce, adjust the salt, and garnish with scallions and cilantro.
tips: Inspired by Cantonese childhood dishes and a recipe by Simone Miller: a one-pan supper with juicy meat and crispy skin.
Dried shiitakes give an 'exponential boost of umami'; soak them at least an hour ahead. Fresh shiitakes work in a pinch.
Save the shiitake stems for bone broth.
Keep the broth and vegetables off the crispy skin.

ai.cliffNotes: Salted thighs seared skin-down until crackly, then roasted in a shallow pool of broth with shallots, shiitakes, ginger and garlic.
keyTips: Salt the thighs while the shallots cook: about 2 teaspoons total, on both sides.
Don't touch the thighs for the full 4 to 5 minutes; that's what makes the skin crisp.
Pour the broth around the chicken, never over it.

recipes.title: Italian Crispy Chicken Thighs

captured.makes: 4 servings · 45 minutes (variation of Cantonese Crispy Chicken Thighs, p.280)
ingredients: Cantonese Crispy Chicken Thighs (p.280) ingredients, with these changes:
thinly sliced fresh cremini mushrooms in place of the dried shiitakes
roughly chopped Italian parsley and basil, for garnish
steps: Follow Cantonese Crispy Chicken Thighs (p.280), substituting thinly sliced fresh cremini for the dried shiitakes and leaving out the ginger in step 8.
In step 15, add a handful of cherry tomatoes to the pan along with the shallots, mushrooms and garlic.
Once out of the oven, garnish with roughly chopped Italian parsley and basil.
tips: SWITCH IT UP from the Cantonese version: for Italian flavors, or when there are no dried shiitakes on hand.
Same technique: sear skin-down until crisp, keep the broth off the skin, roast to 165°F.

ai.cliffNotes: The Cantonese crispy-thigh method with cremini, cherry tomatoes, parsley and basil: Italian flavors, crackly skin, one pan.
keyTips: Fresh cremini need no soaking, so this is the faster version.
The book gives no amount for the cremini; about 6 ounces matches the six dried shiitakes.
